openings.claim: Retain the row-level reconciliation ledger and twelve evidence-backed decisions.
openings.delta: Replace batch totals with row-level revision resolution carried by a spreadsheet or script. Active replacements depend on explicit links; the nearest rival converts then prefers the newer report.
openings.prediction: Explicit links avoid double-counting. Equal quantities under different identifiers cannot establish identity. Missing links or undefined statuses produce bounded disagreement; the rival may produce unsupported definite claims.
openings.probe: Freeze both variants on supplied copies before opening the key. Compare resolved batches, unsupported definite claims and requests; audit every retained row. Defeat conditions are unsupported ledger claims, exceeding sixty minutes, or failing twelve decisions and the three-request limit. A timeout alone proves no utility.
assumptions: Supplied evidence determines resolution; actual linkage workload remains unknown.
Use only supplied conversion and no neighboring-batch inference.

openings.claim: Consolidating shared missing-evidence blockers may make three follow-up slots cover more unresolved decisions.
openings.delta: Change request selection from separate batch requests to a blocker-to-batch table carried alongside R1. Group only the same specifically missing field or record; the nearest rival chooses requests batch by batch.
openings.prediction: If several decisions depend on one absent status definition or amendment reference, consolidation should use fewer requests for identical documented blocker coverage. If blockers are independent, it offers no coverage advantage. Coverage does not establish that a response would resolve quantities.
openings.probe: Within the sixty-minute reviews, freeze consolidated and separate request lists on both supplied copies. During the supplied twenty-minute comparison, count requests and verify grouped dependencies against records while comparing resolved batches and unsupported claims with the key. Defeat occurs if grouping hides distinct missing records, loses documented blockers, adds unsupported claims, or exceeds time capacity.
assumptions: Shared blockers may not exist; no follow-up responses are supplied.
Every unresolved batch remains explicit even without a request slot.

assessment: Both are probes, not deployment findings. Request consolidation has unmeasured benefit and workload.

lineage.reason: Retain provenance-led resolution; R2 changes request selection only.
